author: GitHub
description:
Frances Coronel, a product engineer at Slack, built a personal AI setup to work faster and shared it in a public channel. Engineers across the company started forking it without being asked. That organic pull grew into Slack's internal AI tool catalog: a single source of truth for Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, skills, and GitHub Copilot agents, backed by an adoption dashboard tracking real usage data across teams. In this GitHub Universe 2026 session, Frances demos the catalog, shares six months of real adoption metrics, and shows how a personal productivity hack became org-wide infrastructure. You'll learn how to build an internal AI tool catalog on GitHub with Projects and Issues, measure adoption with real telemetry instead of surveys, and create the cultural conditions that make AI tooling spread on its own.

Speakers: 
Frances Coronel, Senior Software Engineer, Slack 

Watch more videos from GitHub Universe 2026: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AArI948SDz8&list=PLENrlACZ7
title: How a personal AI productivity hack became Slack's internal tool

author: GitHub
description:
Sit down with legendary cybersecurity researcher Niels Provos as he reflects on three decades of breaking, building, and securing software. From sneaking into Canadian university labs to write exportable cryptography and co-authoring bcrypt to protecting billions of users with Google Safe Browsing, Niels shares the core principles behind durable software defense. Discover why he is developing Project Iron Curtain to protect autonomous AI agents against prompt injection and intent drift, and how modern model harnesses are locating decades-old bugs across open-source codebases. Explore his candid thoughts on open-source sustainability, the roots of the word hackathon, and the enduring Cicada 3301 puzzle. 

— CHAPTERS —

title: Niels Provos on creating bcrypt, defending Google, and securing AI agents
